thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: U.S. Stocks Extend Gains As Tech Sector Rallies

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: U.S. Stocks Extend Gains As Tech Sector Rallies
text:
By Sue Chang, MarketWatch , Ryan Vlastelica
Dow gains by triple digits
U.S. stocks rose Tuesday, with the Dow climbing by triple digits, as the technology sector extended gains. Shares had been wobbly earlier as unresolved trade issues continued to dog the market.
Where are the major benchmarks trading?
The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 133 points, or 0.5%, to 25,990. The S&P 500 added 12 points, or 0.4%, to 2,889 with energy, telecom and technology sectors leading the gains. The tech-laden Nasdaq Composite Index advanced 50 points, or 0.6%, to 7,974.
What's driving the market?
Tech shares were among notable gainers with mega-caps Apple Inc. (AAPL), Facebook Inc. (FB) and Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) all rallying.
However, trade worries were simmering below the surface as investors continued to watch the situation between the U.S. and China after President Donald Trump recently threatened China with fresh tariffs. The latest move by Trump would impact an additional $267 billion in Chinese goods, coming on top of an already-proposed $200 billion in tariffs.
China has vowed to retaliate and plans to ask the World Trade Organization next week for permission to impose sanctions on the U.S. for Washington's noncompliance with a ruling in a dispute over U.S. dumping duties, Reuters reported (https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-trade-china-sanctions/china-asks-wto-for-sanctions-in-u-s-trade-dispute-idUSKCN1LR0TM). That's part of a dispute that goes back to 2013.
Investors are worried about a full-on trade war that could have negative implications for global economic growth.
EU and U.S. negotiators met Monday to talk over a pact (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-eu-negotiators-cite-progress-in-latest-discussions-over-trade-2018-09-11)that would avoid a trans-Atlantic spat. Although there was no major breakthrough, U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer and European Trade Commissioner Cecilia Malmström said they would meet up again by the end of September and begin hammering out a deal in the coming months.
Investors are also facing negative seasonal issues, as the month of September is historically the weakest of the year, with an average loss of 1.05% since 1896.
Opinion: Resist the urge to sell if another 9/11-scale attack sinks the stock market (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/resist-the-urge-to-sell-if-another-911-scale-attack-sinks-the-stock-market-2018-09-11)
What are strategists saying?
"You have to watch the trade issue because global supply chains are so complex, and economic growth has depend on the efficiency of these chains," said Tom Plumb, chief investment officer of Plumb Funds.
"Having said that, people talk about the trade issue as though nothing will happen, or as though the worst-case scenario will happen. We think it will be somewhere in between, and while I would stay away from emerging markets and China for a while, we have so much momentum in the U.S. that I would expect any correction to be short lived," he said.
Plumb said he was using the recent weakness as an opportunity to buy stocks like Apple. "Any opportunity to have to buy this at a discount, you'll be well served this year and next," he said.
And:Sell Rosh Hashana, buy Yom Kippur? Here's what the data shows (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/sell-rosh-hashanah-buy-yom-kippur-heres-what-the-data-shows-2018-09-10)
Mike Antonelli, an equity sales trader at Robert W. Baird & Co., credited some of the turnaround to an "oversold bounce" as investors returned to the market to look for bargains after the market's recent losing streak.
Which stocks are in focus?
Yum China Holdings Inc. (YUMC) sank 13% after Bloomberg reported that Hillhouse Capital was dropping its pursuit (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/yum-chinas-stock-plunges-to-pace-nyse-decliners-after-report-suitor-has-dropped-interest-2018-09-11) of operator of Pizza Hut and KFC fast-food restaurants in China.
Shares of Integrated Device Technology Inc.(IDTI) surged 11% after Japan's Renesas Electronics Corp. said it would buy the California-based chip maker in a $6.7 billion deal (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/integrated-device-technology-scooped-up-by-japans-renesas-for-67-billion-2018-09-11).
Sonos Inc. shares fell 19% after the speaker maker's first earnings report since its initial public offering (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/sonos-stock-gives-back-some-of-its-record-gains-after-first-earnings-since-ipo-2018-09-10) showed a net loss and sales that were worse than those reported in the same quarter a year ago. The speaker maker's stock had rallied into the release, soaring 13% in Monday's session.
Tesla Inc. (TSLA) fell 3.5% after it was downgraded by an analyst (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/teslas-stock-drops-after-elon-musks-erratic-behavior-prompts-downgrade-2018-09-11) who cited the "erratic behavior" of Chief Executive Elon Musk.
Sonic Corp.(SONC) surged 9.7% after the fast-food restaurant chain gave an outlook that was above expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/sonics-stock-rallies-after-upbeat-profit-sales-outlook-2018-09-11).
Francesca's Holdings Corp.(FRAN) tumbled 33% and hit all-time lows after the women's clothing chain reported fiscal second-quarter earnings and sales that missed expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/francescas-stock-plunges-toward-record-low-after-profit-and-sales-miss-downbeat-outlook-2018-09-11), and provided a downbeat outlook, citing "weak traffic trends."
MasTec Inc.(MTZ) said it had authorized a new $150 million stock repurchase program (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/mastec-sets-new-150-million-stock-buyback-program-2018-09-11), the largest in the infrastructure construction company's history. Shares rose 1.6%.
Which economic reports are in focus?
Small-business sentiment climbed to a record in August (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/small-business-sentiment-reaches-new-record-in-august-nfib-says-2018-09-11), according to the National Federation of Independent Business. Separately, the number of job openings in the U.S. climbed to a record 6.94 million in July (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-job-openings-climb-to-record-69-million-2018-09-11) while the U.S. budget deficit in August was $211 billion, nearly double the gap during the year-ago period (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-budget-deficit-widens-to-fifth-highest-ever-cbo-reports-2018-09-11).
Fed Governor Lael Brainard and Minneapolis Federal Reserve President Neel Kashkari will speak on a panel about government-sponsored enterprises and housing in the financial crisis at 2:20 p.m. Eastern.
What are other markets doing?
Stocks in Asia had a mostly weaker day (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/nikkei-jumps-but-other-asian-markets-remain-sluggish-2018-09-10) with the exception of Japan's Nikkei 225 index , while European stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/europe-stocks-struggle-with-ftse-100-dragged-by-pound-strength-2018-09-11) were mostly lower.
Oil futures were sharply higher, while gold edged up and the dollar index was flat.
--Barbara Kollmeyer contributed to this report
